Name: Reporting on a hotline for survivors of gender-based violence.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to reporting on a hotline for survivors of gender-based violence
BodyName: Committee on Women and Gender Equity

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Women and Gender Equity
This Introduction was Hearing Held by Committee
History.BodyName: Committee on Women and Gender Equity

History.Description: This Introduction was Laid Over by Committee
History.BodyName: Committee on Women and Gender Equity

Summary: This bill would require the Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (ENDGBV) to report anonymous, high-level information about calls received by ENDGBV’s hotline for survivors of domestic and gender-based violence. ENDGBV would annually report the following about the previous year, disaggregated by month: the number of calls received, the number of calls answered, wait times for calls to be answered, the number of calls that required the use of language interpretation services, the number of requests for placement in a domestic violence shelter, and the borough of origin of the caller, if available.

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:\ulnone\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\qj\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj Section 1. Section 3-181 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by local law number 38 for the year 2019 and redesignated by local law number 109 for the year 2021 and the opening paragraph of such section as amended by a local law for the year 2026, relating to the dates by which reports are transmitted to the council, as proposed in introduction number 1127-C, is amended to read as follows:\par
\'a7 3-181 Reporting on domestic violence initiatives, indicators, and factors. On June 1, 2019, and by March 1 annually thereafter, the office shall submit to the mayor and speaker of the council and post on its website an annual report for the preceding calendar year regarding certain domestic violence initiatives, indicators, and factors. Such report shall include, but need not be limited to:\par
[1.] \ul a.\ulnone  The number of contracted legal service providers providing services in the family justice centers, disaggregated by the primary area of legal practice and languages spoken by the contracted legal service providers, for each family justice center and in total for all family justice centers;\par
[2.] \ul b.\ulnone  The number of contracted service providers providing non-legal services in the family justice centers, disaggregated by type of service, for each family justice center and in total for all family justice centers;\par
[3.] \ul c.\ulnone  The number of family justice center clients, disaggregated by: (i) the total number of client visits, (ii) the total number of unique clients, and (iii) the number of clients accessing each service type, for each family justice center and in total for all family justice centers;\par
[4.] \ul d.\ulnone  A list of all family justice center programs and services offered which pertain to economic empowerment, such as but not limited to those that promote short- and long-term financial planning or navigation of public benefits, disaggregated by type of program or service, for each family justice center and in total for all family justice centers;\par
[5.] \ul e.\ulnone  The total number of outreach events conducted by the office, disaggregated by type of event;\par
[6.] \ul f.\ulnone  The total number of prevention education workshops conducted by the office for youth, staff administering or operating youth programming, or caregivers for youth;\par
[7.] \ul g.\ulnone  The total number of trainings conducted by the office for: (i) city agency staff, (ii) non-profit staff, and (iii) community members; [and]\par
[8.] \ul h. Anonymized information regarding any phone hotline services operated by the office to support survivors of gender-based violence and other crimes, including a description of the kinds of services offered by such hotline during a phone call, disaggregated by the month in which the call occurred, including:\ulnone\par
\ul 1. The total number of calls received;\ulnone\par
\ul 2. The total number of calls answered;\par
3. The average and median wait time for a caller to speak to a hotline operator;\par
4. The number of calls that required the use of language interpretation, disaggregated by language;\ulnone\par
\ul 5. The number of referrals to services made by the hotline;\par
6. The number of requests for placement in a domestic violence shelter received on the hotline;\par
7. The number of single individuals requesting placement in a domestic violence shelter received on the hotline; \par
8. The number of families requesting placement in a domestic violence shelter received on the hotline; and\ulnone\par
\ul 9. The number of calls originating from each borough for calls during which hotline operators request such information after providing services, if practicable; and\par
i.\ulnone  A list of any new data or research reports published by the office.\par
\pard\ltrpar\qj\'a7 2. This local law takes effect March 31, 2027.\fs20\par
